task_value.rationale: A shape policy has a testable path to lower TPOT, and the proposal begins with a cheap inspection of active dispatch and eligible backends. The target bottleneck and baseline delta remain unknown; an unmeasured bottleneck is a valid first falsification question. Transfer inference: pursue the policy only if complete decode traces show a useful backend crossover.

deployment_fit.rationale: The pinned checkpoint format, active MoE backend, second eligible backend, B200 graph compatibility, and DEP8 versus two DEP4 behavior have not been established. The supplied staging code says “ids = tl.where(token_is_padding, -1, ids)” for one NVFP4 path at another commit; it does not establish the pinned path. PR #54520 reports GLM-5.2 on GB300, so its results do not establish DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash compatibility. Warmup and quality risks are identified but unresolved.

discriminating_test.rationale: Inspect resolved dispatch and checkpoint compatibility first; stop if fewer than two correct, graph compatible paths exist. Then trace host time, full MoE time, staging, GEMM, and TPOT; stop if backend choice has no plausible end-to-end headroom. The proposed repeated C1/C4 comparison against unchanged dispatch and the best eligible static backend can distinguish a serving gain from a kernel-only gain. It should also include the target approximately 8K/1K workload at its intended load and compare layouts separately.

evidence_and_limits.rationale: Directly supplied code establishes padding masking in one later staging path, not target performance. Author claims: PR #57977 reports “C1 ×3 TPOT | 6.58 / 6.58 / 6.58 ms | 6.50 / 6.50 / 6.50 ms” for a different change; PR #54520 reports backend throughput on GB300 with GLM-5.2. The EPS-MoE full-text excerpt says “switching from GroupedGemm to DenseGemm at a certain token number”; that supports prior use of shape selection, not this implementation. Transfer inference is conditional. Target effect size, bottleneck, active backend, and relevant limitations remain unknown.

objections: No supplied target trace shows that expert GEMM, rather than host scheduling, routing, staging, or communication, limits TPOT.
A second backend may be ineligible for the pinned weight format or graph mode; PR and paper results do not settle this.
The proposed C1/C4 study alone would not establish value for the approximately 8K input / 1K output target workload at its intended load.
The prior rejection for lack of novelty is not a veto under this rubric.
reviews.required_revision: Keep R1 as a conditional candidate. State the resolved checkpoint, backend, graph mode, and eligible paths before implementation; add a matched target-workload serving point for each relevant eight-GPU layout, with output quality and startup cost alongside TPOT.

global_gaps: The supplied material does not resolve the active backend, MTP/DSpark state, or DEP8 versus two DEP4 configuration at the pinned deployment.
No target decode trace establishes MoE share of TPOT, routed-row distribution, or backend crossover.
The reported 27.6882 req/s point is an author-reported aggregate without a kernel, rank, or request trace; the 75% cacheability target is not a measured hit rate.
